label: D1 after rare a1->S2 rewarded; also a2 S2 r following a1 S1 u
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 r") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (tv("reward",-2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * ((tv("action",-2) == 1) & (tv("state",-2) == 1) & (tv("reward",-2) == 0)) ;; (phase != D1)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (zero at GO/D2). Magnitude is set by the previous trial: after a1 -> S2 rewarded (rare transition, rewarded) it is ~+2.7 above timing, slightly lower (~-0.26) if the trial before that was also rewarded. After a common a2 -> S2 rewarded trial it is weak (~+0.2) unless the trial before was a1 -> S1 unrewarded (i.e. the agent switched to a2 and got rewarded at S2), which adds ~+1.8. All other previous-trial patterns give ~0. Only observed history is used; hidden good state, since_rev, value/policy and future variables add nothing beyond this. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.70 (dev 0.71) vs all ceiling 0.72; last trial alone reference 0.66.

issues: The main claims hold. The feature fires only at D1 (GO and D2 are exactly 0 in the profile). The previous trial a1 S2 r drives it (residual +2.44, weight +2.71). Test R^2 beyond timing reproduces at 0.7005, against an 'all' ceiling of 0.72.

The claim that a1->S2 rewarded is 'about 0.26 lower if the trial before was also rewarded' averages over very different cases. Splitting by the trial-before pattern gives these test-fit weights: after a2 S2 r -2.33, after a2 S1 r -1.27, after a1 S2 r -1.22, after a1 S1 r -0.04 (about 0), after a1 S2 u +0.57. So the drop happens when the trial before was a rewarded S2 visit or a rewarded a2 trial, not after rewards in general. One worst-fit dev window shows a1 S2 r following a1 S2 r at 1.79 actual against 2.70 predicted.

The claim that a2->S2 rewarded is weak 'unless the trial before was a1 -> S1 unrewarded' is too narrow. It is raised whenever the trial before was any a1 trial: a1 S1 u +1.84, a1 S1 r +0.76, a1 S2 u +0.91, a1 S2 r +0.51. a2 S2 u also gives +0.47. A dev miss shows a2 S2 r after a2 S2 u at 2.33 actual against 0.27 predicted. The general effect is 'a2 S2 r right after a switch away from a1', strongest after a1 S1 u, not one single pattern.
The (phase != D1) term adds about 0.03 R^2 (0.6726 without it, 0.7005 with it). It acts as a lower D1 offset for all non-target patterns. That shape is fine, but the explanation does not mention it.

Misses on the original terms show no large systematic phase or pattern error. The largest is the first trial of a window, where the previous trial is unknown ('?'): +0.085. Better terms only improve test R^2 from 0.700 to 0.719, so the gap is in how the explanation describes the two-back modulation, not in fit.
